This consistent layout makes it easy for a chatbot to retrieve the right answer for a farmer’s question. Important note: amounts, subsidy rates and deadlines change from time to time and states may add their own top-up. The chatbot should advise farmers to confirm current details on the official website or with the Kisan Call Centre (1800-180-1551) before applying. This is an information guide, not an official government notification.

The Union Cabinet approved continuation of the scheme from 2026-27 to 2030-31. Indian Agriculture Schemes - Farmer Knowledge Base (updated November 2026) Page 8 Scheme 2: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) Category: Crop Insurance Ministry / Department: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare Launched: Kharif 2016 Objective Low-premium crop insurance against crop loss from natural calamities, pests and diseases. Benefits  Farmer premium is capped at 2% of sum insured for Kharif food and oilseed crops, 1.5% for Rabi food and oilseed crops, and 5% for annual commercial and horticultural crops. The rest is paid by the Centre and the State.  Covers: prevented or failed sowing, standing crop loss (yield loss), post-harvest losses up to 14 days for crops kept to dry in the field (cyclone, unseasonal rain), and localized calamities such as hailstorm, landslide, inundation, cloudburst and natural fire.  Claim money is paid directly into the farmer’s bank account. Eligibility  All farmers, including sharecroppers and tenant farmers, growing notified crops in

Eligibility  All farmers, including sharecroppers and tenant farmers, growing notified crops in notified areas.  Voluntary for all farmers since Kharif 2020 (loanee farmers can opt out by giving a written declaration to their bank before the cut-off date). How to Apply  Through your bank (for KCC/loanee farmers), a Common Service Centre, an authorised insurance company agent, or directly on pmfby.gov.in.  Enrol before the state’s cut-off date (usually around 31 July for Kharif and 31 December for Rabi, but dates vary by state and crop).  Report localized or post-harvest crop loss within 72 hours on the Crop Insurance app, helpline 14447, the insurance company, or the bank / agriculture office. Documents Required  Aadhaar card  Bank passbook  Land record (RoR / Khatauni) or tenancy/sharecropping agreement  Sowing certificate (from Patwari/sarpanch, as required by state)

Documents Required  Aadhaar card  Bank passbook  Land record (RoR / Khatauni) or tenancy/sharecropping agreement  Sowing certificate (from Patwari/sarpanch, as required by state) Official Website / Helpline Website: pmfby.gov.in | Helpline: 14447 | App: Crop Insurance (Android) Frequently Asked Questions - Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana Q: How much premium do I pay under PMFBY? A: 2% for Kharif crops, 1.5% for Rabi crops, and 5% for commercial/horticultural crops, calculated on the sum insured. Q: What should I do if my crop is damaged by hailstorm? A: Inform the insurance company within 72 hours through the Crop Insurance app, helpline 14447, or your bank/agriculture office, giving crop, area and survey number. Q: Is PMFBY compulsory for KCC holders? A: No. Since Kharif 2020 it is voluntary. A loanee farmer who does not want it must give a written opt-out to the bank before the cut-off date.

Indian Agriculture Schemes - Farmer Knowledge Base (updated November 2026) Page 9 Scheme 3: Restructured Weather Based Crop Insurance Scheme (RWBCIS) Category: Crop Insurance Ministry / Department: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare Launched: Kharif 2016 Objective Insurance that pays based on weather parameters (rainfall, temperature, humidity, wind) instead of measured yield loss. Benefits  Same farmer premium as PMFBY: 2% Kharif, 1.5% Rabi, 5% commercial/horticultural crops.  Payout is triggered automatically when recorded weather deviates from the notified ’normal’ at the reference weather station, so no crop-cutting experiments are needed. Eligibility  All farmers including tenants and sharecroppers growing notified crops in areas where the state has notified RWBCIS. How to Apply  Same as PMFBY: bank, CSC, insurance agent or pmfby.gov.in, before the notified cut-off date. Documents Required  Aadhaar card  Bank passbook  Land record or tenancy agreement Official

ow to Apply  Same as PMFBY: bank, CSC, insurance agent or pmfby.gov.in, before the notified cut-off date. Documents Required  Aadhaar card  Bank passbook  Land record or tenancy agreement Official Website / Helpline Website: pmfby.gov.in | Helpline: 14447 Frequently Asked Questions - Restructured Weather Based Crop Insurance Scheme Q: What is the difference between PMFBY and RWBCIS? A: PMFBY pays based on actual yield loss assessed in the field; RWBCIS pays when weather data (rain, temperature etc.) crosses fixed limits. The state decides which one applies to a crop and area.

Indian Agriculture Schemes - Farmer Knowledge Base (updated November 2026) Page 10 Scheme 4: Kisan Credit Card (KCC) Scheme Category: Credit / Loans Ministry / Department: Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, RBI and NABARD Launched: August 1998 (extended to animal husbandry and fisheries in 2018-19) Objective Timely and cheap short-term credit for crop cultivation, post-harvest needs, household consumption, farm assets maintenance, and allied activities. Benefits  Short-term crop loans at 7% interest per year; with the 3% Prompt Repayment Incentive (PRI) the effective rate becomes 4% per year.  Loan limit eligible for interest subvention raised from Rs. 3 lakh to Rs. 5 lakh (announced in Union Budget 2025-26).  Collateral-free (no security) loans up to Rs. 2 lakh from 1 January 2025 (earlier Rs. 1.6 lakh).  RuPay debit card for withdrawals; card valid for 5 years with yearly review; revolving cash credit.  Available for fishermen, fish farmers and

Rs. 2 lakh from 1 January 2025 (earlier Rs. 1.6 lakh).  RuPay debit card for withdrawals; card valid for 5 years with yearly review; revolving cash credit.  Available for fishermen, fish farmers and dairy / poultry / animal husbandry farmers too. Eligibility  Owner-cultivators, tenant farmers, oral lessees, sharecroppers.  Self-Help Groups (SHGs) and Joint Liability Groups (JLGs) of farmers.  Fishers, fish farmers and livestock farmers. ntity proof (Aadhaar, Voter ID, PAN etc.)  Address proof  Land records / cropping pattern details  Passport-size photograph Official Website / Helpline Contact your bank branch | Kisan Call Centre: 1800-180-1551 Frequently Asked Questions - Kisan Credit Card Q: What is the interest rate on a KCC loan? A: 7% per year for loans under the interest subvention limit; if repaid on time you get 3% back, so the effective rate is 4%. Q: Do I need to give security for a KCC loan? A: No security is needed for loans up to Rs. 2 lakh. Q: Can a dairy farmer get a KCC? A: Yes. KCC is available for animal husbandry, dairy, poultry and fisheries activities.

Indian Agriculture Schemes - Farmer Knowledge Base (updated November 2026) Page 12 Scheme 6: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maandhan Yojana (PM-KMY) Category: Pension / Social Security Ministry / Department: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (administered by LIC) Launched: 12 September 2019 Objective Old-age pension for small and marginal farmers. Benefits  Assured pension of Rs. 3,000 per month after age 60.  Farmer pays a monthly contribution of Rs. 55 to Rs. 200 (depending on entry age); the Central Government pays an equal amount.  If the farmer dies after 60, the spouse gets 50% (Rs. 1,500 per month) as family pension.  Contribution can be auto-deducted from PM-KISAN benefit if the farmer chooses. Eligibility  Small and marginal farmers aged 18 to 40 years holding up to 2 hectares of cultivable land.  NOT eligible: persons covered under NPS, ESIC, EPFO or other statutory pension schemes; income tax payers; those in PM-SYM or PM-LVM. Documents Required  Aadhaar card  Savings bank account / IFSC  Land record Official Website / Helpline Website: maandhan.in | Helpline: 1800-267-6888 Frequently Asked Questions - Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maandhan Yojana Q: How much do I need to pay for PM Kisan Maandhan?
